chapter_theme: Women who sell intimacy are portrayed as a danger to men because their words and embrace are divided from their hearts. The chapter's argument is that the falseness is detectable, and that who touches them reveals the quality of the man. It gives no view from the women's side.
structure_note: Parimelazhagar: their words and acts are false (911-913), the high-minded will not touch them (914-916), and those who do are the low (917-920). He notes that 920 pairs them with drink and dice to introduce the next two chapters.

911.reading: The sweet words of bangled women who desire a man for his wealth and not from love will bring him harm.
911.nuance: The harm is located in the sweet speech, not the sex. The chapter opens as a chapter on deceptive language.

912.reading: Weigh the conduct of faithless women who weigh the profit and then speak of their own virtue, and keep away from them.
912.nuance: தூக்கி is repeated: she weighs the gain, so he must weigh her in return. Parimelazhagar calls this behaviour their சாதி தருமம், which is a commentator's social classification and not in the verse.

positions.position: நயன் is their conduct, examined so that one can leave them.
நயன் is the pleasure they offer, which on examination is not worth approaching.

913.reading: The false embrace of women of wealth is like embracing a stranger's corpse in a dark room.
913.nuance: A quick reader takes the client to be holding a corpse, as Pope's couplet does. Parimelazhagar and Kalaignar make the woman the embracer: she is the hired bearer, and the unwanted client is the corpse she handles for pay. On that reading the disgust is hers, which complicates the chapter's usual stance.

positions.position: The image describes her inner state: outwardly embracing, inwardly recoiling for the sake of money, like a paid corpse-bearer.
positions.quote: அகத்தால் அருவராநின்றும் பொருள் நோக்கிப் புறத்தால் தழுவுவர்

positions.position: She embraces someone for money and acts out false love.
positions.quote: பணத்துக்காக மட்டுமே ஒருவரைத் தழுவிப் பொய்யன்பு காட்டி நடிப்பது

914.reading: Those whose understanding weighs the wealth of grace will not plunge into the base charms of women whose wealth is only wealth.

positions.position: அருட்பொருள் is wealth joined to grace: the wise still pursue wealth, but examine how to use it graciously.
positions.quote: அருளொடு கூடிய பொருளை ஆராய்ந்து செய்யும் அறிவினையுடையார்

positions.position: அருட்பொருள் treats grace itself as the wealth one seeks.

915.reading: Those whose knowledge has been refined by the goodness of their intellect will not plunge into the base charms of those whose goodness belongs to everyone.
915.nuance: பொதுநலம், 'common goodness', is a pointed phrase, since நலம் elsewhere means personal excellence. Parimelazhagar explains மதிநலம் as clarity earned in former births; the verse names no births.

916.reading: Those who would spread their own goodness will not touch the shoulders of women who, proud of their charm, spread a base goodness.
916.nuance: The same verb பாரிப்பார் is used for both parties: each is spreading a நலம், and the verse sets reputation against availability as two kinds of publicity.

917.reading: Those with no firmness of heart touch the shoulders of women who join with them while tending other things in their hearts.
917.nuance: A divided heart on one side is paired with an unguarded heart on the other. The verse's பிற is unspecified; the commentators fill it with wealth.

918.reading: For those lacking discerning understanding, the embrace of deceiving women is said to be an அணங்கு.

positions.position: அணங்கு is a divine woman who takes life through desire, so the embrace is sweet and then fatal.
அணங்கு simply means affliction, with no divine being.

919.reading: The soft shoulders of women of fine jewels who draw no line are the mire in which base men with no worth sink.
919.nuance: வரைவு, 'limit', gives the chapter its title. Parimelazhagar says it means no line between high and low clients, and insists பூரியர் here means low in understanding, not in caste. அளறு means hell and mire at once, and softness of shoulder fits sinking.

920.reading: Double-minded women, liquor and dice are the company of those whom Fortune has cast off.

positions.position: These companions are signs by which one can tell that the goddess has already abandoned a man.
Consorting with them is what causes life's distinction to depart.
positions.quote: தொடர்பு கொண்டு உழல்வோரை விட்டு வாழ்வில் அமைய வேண்டிய சிறப்பு அகன்றுவிடும்.

links.note: 91 defines இன்சொல் as speech soaked in love and free of guile. 911 shows what is left when love is removed: the same sweetness becomes the instrument of harm. So the Kural's praise of sweet speech was never about sweetness alone.

241 ranks the wealth of grace above material wealth, which even the பூரியார் have. 914 applies the same contrast to choice of company, and 919's பூரியர் are the ones who sink, so these verses share a vocabulary of grace against base wealth.

Both tie a man's நலம் to whose shoulders he doesn't touch, using the same verb தோய். 149 says it of another's wife and 916 of women who sell themselves, so the two forbidden categories are treated in one idiom of self-possession.
Fortune as a goddess who leaves or stays: 617 places her at the feet of the unidle man, and 920 says the ones she has dropped can be known by their company.

source_issues: 913: Pope's couplet makes the client the one embracing the corpse, while Parimelazhagar and Kalaignar make the woman the embracer; Pope's gloss mentions 'hired men', drawn from Parimelazhagar.
